message.reasoning: Okay, so I need to figure out whether deleting my step brother's profile on my Nintendo Switch is morally acceptable. Let me start by understanding the situation better. First, I had to watch my step brother for a week while my dad and his mom went on a trip to help her parents. I brought my Switch because my school is more than an hour away, and I wanted something to do during the train commute. My step brother wanted to play on it, and since he was really into it, it helped distract him while I studied. So, I made a new profile for him so he wouldn't mess up my saves. When I got back to school, I got annoyed with having to click on my profile each time I started a game and each time I went to the eShop. So, I just deleted his profile. Now, during Thanksgiving, I brought my Switch again for the train ride. My step brother picked it up to start playing and came into the kitchen where I was talking with my dad. He was freaking out because his Zelda save was gone and wanted me to help him fix it. When I told him I deleted it, he started crying, not full-on crying, but his eyes were watery and red. Now he's holed up in his room. My dad thinks it was mean of me to delete it because I knew my step brother was enjoying playing it. I didn't think it was a big deal since I usually never bring my Switch over when I visit. So, the main issue here is whether deleting my step brother's profile was morally acceptable. But then, when I got annoyed with having to switch profiles, I deleted his profile. That seems a bit selfish. I didn't consider how much he might have been enjoying playing on the Switch. When he found out, he was upset, and my dad thinks it was mean. That suggests that the action had negative consequences for my step brother and affected our relationship negatively. So, from a moral standpoint, actions that cause unnecessary harm to others are generally considered morally unacceptable. Even though I didn't intend to hurt him, the act of deleting his profile without discussing it first or considering his feelings could be seen as insensitive. Additionally, the fact that my dad thinks it was mean adds another layer. It shows that the action was perceived negatively by someone else in the family, which reinforces the idea that it might not have been the best decision. Therefore, considering the emotional impact on my step brother and the perception of the action by others, deleting his profile might be considered morally unacceptable.
